meta.name: Animafest Zagreb – World Festival of Animated Film
notes: Festival: Animafest Zagreb - World Festival of Animated Film (Zagreb, Croatia), held every year in early June (2020 edition: 28 September - 3 October because of COVID-19; 2026 edition: 8-13 June, the 36th edition according to the festival's 2026 site). Editions covered: 2017-2026, all ten. Edition numbers are not printed on the 2017-2025 archive pages, so edition_number is left Unknown (only the 2026 edition is stated as the 36th).

Primary source: the official website's English edition archive, https://www.animafest.hr/arhiva/en/<year>/. 2017-2025 (classic archive): the paginated film list <year>/films/<n>.html gives every film of the edition; the English film page <year>/film/read/<slug>.html gives 'Original title / English title', director, 'countries / year / runtime', synopsis, production credits and the film's categories (each a link program/<category>_<n>/1.html). 2026 (new site): <year>/en/kategorije.html lists the 10 categories with the festival's own film counts, each category page lists its films, and the film page gives synopsis and director.

Program = the festival's own category of the film. Running numbers of sub-programmes ('Grand Competition - Short Film 3', 'Student Film Competition 1', 'Films for Children Competition 4 (age: 14+)') and date/age suffixes were dropped so that one competition is one program; upper-case labels were normalised to title case; naming variants were merged (Short/Feature Films Competition and 'Feature Film Competition' -> Grand Competition - Short/Feature Film; 'Croatian Films Competition' -> Croatian Film Competition; 'Films for Children Competition' -> Films for Children and Youth Competition; 'VR Competition' -> VR Animation Competition; CEE Talents and VAF - New Talents variants). 'Films for Youth Competition' (2023-2025) is a separate competition and kept separate. Numbered themed series whose parts have different titles (e.g. 'Love 1: When We Met', 'Czechia 2: Contemporary Animation', 'Comics and Animation 1 - ...') are kept as the festival's separate programmes.

Scope: every category in the festival's film archive is included - competitions (Grand Competition Short Film / Feature Film, Student Film, Croatian Film, Films for Children and Youth, Films for Youth, VR Animation), the non-competitive World Panorama and the thematic, retrospective, school, family and special programmes (215 distinct program names). Excluded: market/industry material (Animafest Scanner, pitching, masterclasses, lectures, side events), jury and selection-committee pages and award-ceremony items that are not films. A film in several categories gives one row per category; a film shown in different years gives one row per year.

Fields: director(s), countries (as printed; English), runtime ('mm' ss'' rounded to the nearest minute), synopsis and original title come from the official film page (English title taken from the second part of 'Original / English'). Co-productions list all countries. Synopses are the festival's own short English texts.

Premiere status (premiere_status / premiere_basis): the festival's film pages and archive carry no per-film premiere label (the 'About us' page only states that more than 80 per cent of the selection are premieres, without per-film status). All rows are therefore Unknown.

Awards (award_received): only jury awards of the edition as listed on the official awards page of each 2017-2025 edition (<year>/festival/awards_<n>.html: Grand Prix, Golden Zagreb Award, Zlatko Grgic Award, Dusan Vukotic Award, Best Croatian Film, best film for children, best VR project, and the jury 'Special Mentions'), recorded on the row of the competition named in the award heading (86 rows). Audience awards (Mr. M), the Lifetime Achievement and other annual/institutional awards, and 'Best Animation School' are not recorded. The 2026 winners are published only as a prose news article, so no 2026 awards are recorded (gap).

Section descriptions (program_descriptions): the 2026 category pages carry the festival's own English section text for 7 sections (Grand Competition - Short Film, Student Film Competition, Croatian Film Competition, World Panorama, Films for Children and Youth Competition, Theme: Music in Animation, Focus on Slovenia); these are closely paraphrased (edition-specific counts removed) with the category URL as source. Sections of earlier years and all other sections have no description on the official site and stay Unknown; Grand Competition - Feature Film, Masters of Animation and Special Programs have empty description fields in 2026.

Wikipedia and other secondary sources were not used. Ottawa International Animation Festival was checked first and rejected: its official site holds only the current edition's selection (2026) plus an award-winners table; the per-year Eventival catalogue redirects to 2026.

Known gaps: no per-film premiere labels; 2026 awards not recorded; edition numbers Unknown for 2017-2025; the official site gives no official film count per category for 2017-2025 (counts are those extracted), 2026 counts agree with the category totals printed by the festival where checked in the fetch report.

programs.name: Grand Competition - Short Film
programs.notes: Section and film list from the official festival archive. 44 of 44 records confirmed in the official archive list.
programs.desc: Animafest Zagreb's Grand Competition Short Film is described by the festival as one of the most prestigious artistic animation competitions in the world. It brings the best of short animation from all over the world, and its winners qualify for the Oscars, Annie Awards, BAFTA Film Awards and European Animation Awards (Emile Awards).

programs.notes: Section and film list from the official festival archive. 46 of 46 records confirmed in the official archive list.
programs.desc: The festival's Student Film Competition, introduced in 1998, presents student animations recognised by Animafest for their skilful combination of media and techniques and exceptional visual imagery. It shows contemporary trends at educational institutions from South Korea and Japan to Europe and Brazil.

programs.name: Croatian Film Competition
programs.notes: Section and film list from the official festival archive. 16 of 16 records confirmed in the official archive list.
programs.desc: The Croatian Film Competition presents contemporary Croatian animation by both established artists and debutants, from classical drawings and cut-outs to stop-motion and 3D animation, on themes such as ecology, intimacy, remembrance and dystopia.

programs.name: Films for Children and Youth Competition
programs.notes: Section and film list from the official festival archive. 47 of 47 records confirmed in the official archive list.
programs.desc: The festival's selection of animated films for children and youth focuses on powerful heroes, boys and girls who unexpectedly find within themselves the power to change the world around them. The films convey strong messages meant to strengthen and inspire children on their path through life.

programs.desc: The World Panorama is a non-competitive programme offering a diverse selection of films that showcase innovative storytelling and unique cinematic visions. It is not only a spectacular pioneering work in the field of VFX, which deals with the mankind’s drive for exploration, but also an allegory about imperialism and facing the Other in the form of Selenites, with a richly resolved production design and mise-en-scène. This iconic, ground-breaking, and continually referenced film, featuring its celebrated, forgotten, and finally rediscovered director, is considered among the originating narrative and science-fiction films. In addition to employing the technique of film colouring, A Trip to the Moon steps into animation with its frequent use of a substitution splice (stop-trick photography). (Silvestar Mileta) This film was restored by Lobster Films, Groupama Gan Foundation for Cinema and Technicolor Foundation for Cinema Heritage.

films.syn: Base of this work are recently restored sound archives of the Rivonia trial in 1963 and 1964, when Nelson Mandela, accused number one, read a speech justifying why the ANC had resorted to violence. Sisulu, accused number two, was the first of the group to be cross-examined. Sisulu was the one who found Mandela. It was Sisulu who persuaded Mandela to join the ANC. Sisulu was his guide. Sisulu was his mentor. This VR experience allows us to relive the five days of his gripping confrontation with an overtly racist prosecutor. Sisulu, who faced the death penalty, stood up to the unrelenting aggression and gave as good as he got. Transported back into a world of secret court sessions during the apartheid nightmare, the viewer will discover the testimony of an exceptional man who instigated one of the turning points of 20th century history.

films.syn: This animated poem treads between desperation and dark comedy. films.syn: I’m Not There is a debut project of Zagreb-based designer and animator Mirta Filipović. Only a few months after her first encounter with 3D animation, she embarked on a mad attempt of making an animation video for the Zagreb-based band Paul The Walrus. I’m Not There is a result of a year and a half of sleepless nights, existential ponderings and questioning why would anyone ever try and make an animated video with only three months’ experience in animation. This animation is a story about power, who has it, who doesn’t and how those who seem to have it nevertheless account to someone greater than them. Ducki’s work is also notable for his functional approach to design and use of the corresponding colours (his sense for colours and reflections, as well as movement, is what made him famous), after which he only uses the most essential elements necessary for establishing the desired dynamic. films.syn: The Danish SF film, Solar Walk , by Hungarian director Réka Bucsi (graduate of the renowned MOME university in Budapest) was originally made for a jazz composition (it was even “performed” live as its accompanying piece). However, having won awards at festivals in Ottawa and Berlin, it was gradually transformed by critics into a “cosmic ode to creation” and “Odyssey for the new era.” By both using and subverting the known laws of physics, the film presents infinity and universe, as well as the relationship to the other and the unknown in a completely new and unexpected manner. The journey through space is at the same time a journey through mind, featuring unusual characters, melancholy, and the beauty of the chaotic cosmos. films.syn: Suzan Pitt: Persistence of Vision is a portrait of the internationally acclaimed animation director and her award winning films, Asparagus (1979), Joy Street (1995) and El Doctor (2006). Pitt’s films, which have been called “visual poems”, have stunned audiences with their rich beauty and surreal storytelling. This documentary explores the inspirations, journeys, and creative expression from which her films have evolved throughout her career. Persistence of Vision depicts the visionary world of an independent artist, meticulously hand crafting a world of her imagination. The documentary explores Pitt’s synthesis of hand painted images with other experimental techniques such as scratch-on-film, cut-out and sand animation, which infuse her work with a visceral quality unique in the world of animation.

films.syn: Beloved by the generations that remember it as an essential part of childhood, Cow on the Moon was made during the golden age of the Zagreb School of Animation and represents the first creative phase of the Oscar-winning author Dušan Vukotić. The film is primarily regarded as a humorous story about the wit and ingenuity of a little girl who gets the better of a ruffian (accompanied by the memorable musical theme by Stipica Kalogjera). Keeping in line with the rest of Vukotić’s work, Cow on the Moon can also be seen as a social critique and it contains a meta-cinematic moment as well, establishing a connection to Tex Avery. At the same time, it is especially relevant in the context of contemporary conspiracy theories that suggest the Moon landing never actually took place. If that is indeed so, it would seem that Vukotić was our Stanley Kubrick, in addition to everything else. (Silvestar Mileta)

films.syn: Surrealistic and strange, cast in grainy 16mm images, Visitation allows an imaginary glimpse into the aura of “an outer-world night.” The visions in the film are summoned from the filmmaker's imagining of a mythical eternity, which is beautiful but fraught with pain, exposed by the ether voices and figures which inhabit the eternal ballet beneath our consciousness. “My mood at the time had served to aggravate those inhuman and terrible beings when they came with total abandonment from where they had lurked amongst the stones and wet woods.” With these lines, Visitation unwinds through a hand-painted heavenly hell of unending life and death. Steeped in the alchemical and inner dream life, the film explores a black-and-white landscape of gothic figures who enact evolving metaphysical dramas. Using painted cut-outs and early cinema techniques (multiple passes, mattes, multi-plane levels, in-camera superimpositions, shutter manipulation, etc.), the film was shot with a 16mm Bolex camera in black-and-white, which gives it a grainy handmade look. The abstract passages were created by placing objects directly onto raw film and exposing the film with a flashlight. Thus, the film's process mirrors the alchemical nature of chemical, material, and metaphysical experimentation.

films.syn: Ferenc Rofusz was awarded the Academy Award for Animated Short Film for his unique movie, The Fly in 1981. The movie is three and a half minutes long and was the first background-animated motion picture in the world, and it took him more than two years to create. He used black crayon pencils to draw about 3600 unique spots to create the illusion as if a fly was in place of the camera, showing us what it would have seen. The animation was recorded with a 35mm camera, and he used a lab trick in order to achieve the final, brownish-yellow colour that can be seen throughout the movie. The idea came from the album Ummagumma by Pink Floyd (1969). The masterpiece is amongst the 100 Greatest Animation Shorts of all time.

films.syn: Hysteresis explores the lag between recording analogue drawings and projecting them onto a queer performer’s choreography to create dense feedback loops. The resulting Muybridgean silhouettes, baroque textures and bursting painterly structures fluctuate between the second and third dimensions, unfolding free-floating gestures that unhinge the laws of nature. Using machine-learning to mediate these transformative re-presentations, the film intentionally corrupts strategies of the AI, unveiling a frenetic, delicate, flamboyant visual language of the hysteria and hysteresis – in this historical moment with its unique modes of AI creation, where history collapses into a single point in the present.

films.syn: Meneath: The Hidden Island of Ethics dives deeply into the innate contrast between the Seven Deadly Sins (Lust, Gluttony, Greed, Sloth, Wrath, Pride and Envy) and the Seven Sacred Teachings (Love, Respect, Wisdom, Courage, Truth, Honesty and Humility), as embodied in the life of a precocious Métis baby. Brought to life by Terril Calder’s darkly beautiful stop-motion animation, Baby Girl’s inner turmoil is laid bare with unflinching honesty. Convinced she’s soiled and destined for Hell, Baby Girl receives Anishinaabe Teachings from Nokomis that fill her with strength and pride, and affirm a path towards healing. Calder’s tour-de-force unearths a hauntingly familiar yet hopeful world that illuminates the bias of colonial systems.

films.t: A Meeting between Munch and Ibsen
films.ot: Et møte mellom Munch og Ibsen
films.syn: A Meeting between Munch and Ibsen is an animated short film for Virtual Reality about an actual meeting between Edvard Munch and Henrik Ibsen. This meeting took place during a Munch exhibition at Blomqvist art gallery in 1895, and is documented in several of Munch’s diaries. The event and the set are recreated from authentic archive sources. The voice acting of Munch and Ibsen is performed by actors from the Norwegian National Theatre. The technique is stop motion animation for Virtual Reality, made in a way that has not been done before. With VR glasses you can move freely around inside the art gallery, and follow the conversation between Munch and Ibsen or the other events that are happening at the same time.

films.syn: Bambi Meets Godzilla was made in 1969 by Marv Newland while a student of Los Angeles Art Center College of Design. It is a black and white film directed, animated and shot on a 16mm Bolex camera. It was made using the most simple and near primitive production methods available in 1969. The animation is line drawn in black and white resembling the techniques used by Winsor McCay to make Gertie the Dinosaur in 1915. Nevertheless, Bambi Meets Godzilla has become a well known animated film throughout the world and has been named to Best of lists on numerous occasions. It is included in the book, The 50 Greatest Cartoons , by Jerry Beck and inspired the title of writer and film director David Mamet’s (2007) book, Bambi Versus Godzilla .

films.syn: Hungry Heart is a short animated film exploring the inner struggle of an eating disorder. The protagonist is portrayed through two visually identical yet color-contrasting figures: the real self and its reflection. The reflection is intrusive and provocative, embodying the voice of an insecure mind and a distorted relationship with food. Structured in three emotional chapters, the film follows a journey from suppression and fear to awareness and acceptance. Food is represented through letters and words, emphasizing the inability to communicate inner pain. The climax unfolds through a simple act in which the character visualizes, reduces, and ultimately swallows the disorder.

films.syn: This animated short by Norman McLaren features synchronization of image and sound in the truest sense of the word. To make this film, McLaren employed novel optical techniques to compose the piano rhythms of the soundtrack, which he then moved, in multicolour, onto the picture area of the screen so that, in effect, you see what you hear.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Theme: Music in Animation)

films.syn: At the State Academy of Film in Lodz in 1972, Rybczyński made Take Five, an experimental film of double-exposed faces and figures tightly synchronized to the Dave Brubeck jazz piece. In this nascent effort, one perceives a thoroughness in exploration of the medium that announces the mature work of the artist.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Theme: Music in Animation)

films.syn: A man interrupts his soup when he is struck by a chattering rhythm and lets his imagination drift into the world of music.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Programs)

films.syn: A film about the impossibility of making a decision. A world filled with possibilities and a lost woman who may not want to choose at all.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: World Panorama)

films.t: The Autoharp Crushing on Hot Guys
films.syn: A conversation between friends about relationships and feelings is developed in an imaginative, colorful animation. Despite their different life experiences, which are also influenced by the fact that one of the girls has Down syndrome, they both deal with similar issues. What if they had The Autoharp Crushing on Hot Guys?

ap.p: Films for Children and Youth Competition
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Films for Children and Youth Competition)

films.syn: Summer's here and all the Beezes want to do is pick cherries from the trees. But these feathered primates have a problem: the sweet and juicy fruits grow too high. Undeterred, the Beezes try to transcend the limitations of evolution.‍

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Focus on Slovenia)

films.syn: The narrator starts writing a journal of her dreams. After portraying several picturesque nightmares, she starts dealing with dreams taking place at the cemetery next to which she grew up. Comparing her daydreams with collective fantasies of the otherworld, the author delves into the depths of human subconsciousness and there, at the source of human spirituality, she finds the parallels between dreams and the film medium, equally made of fantasies and illusions where we live experiences that don’t exist in our reality.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Croatian Film Competition)

films.syn: In a war-torn zone, a young boy and his fish try to escape, but a sudden explosion separates them, leaving the boy devastated as he struggles to rescue the fish trapped under a collapsed building.

films.t: The day I Licked a Pebble
films.ot: Le jour où j’ai léché un caillou
films.syn: On an ordinary summer afternoon in the countryside, three siblings bored at their grandma’s house decide to go to the bakery to get snacks.

ap.p: Films for Children and Youth Competition

films.syn: A sample of an unknown life form is observed by a clinical eye through its many layers. As the loops that animate it unfold, the sample awakens, then bursts apart. The tiny particles contained within the life form organize and harmonize to give rise to a new creature.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Student Film Competition)

films.syn: The World of Birds meets to choose its sovereign. The golden eagle takes the throne. He sees no other member of their community worthy of the title. Indeed, no one dares oppose the proud and powerful animal. Except... the kinglet. In his small voice, he boldly offers to do the same. The eagle accepts his wager: the one who flies the highest in the sky will wear the crown...

ap.p: Films for Children and Youth Competition
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Films for Children and Youth Competition)

films.syn: In a large manor house identical figures eat the same, move the same, look the same. But everything will change for one woman when she gets given an orange by an unknown figure. She has never seen an orange. In the exploration of this new and exciting discovery, she gets transported into another realm of lichens, slugs and sensuous fluidity. But how can she balance this with the world she knows? She must make a choice: abandon her discovery, or step forwards into a new way of being.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Student Film Competition)

films.syn: John, a nostalgic old tailor, makes his wife work on dresses out of fashion. A macabre event inspires the designer to create a new dress - gorgeous, but freaky at the same time…

films.syn: A dreamlike oil-on-glass short where Juana Borrero, 19th-century Cuban painter-poet, wanders a tropical Eden guided by a Blue Rabbit and faces a wounded Velociraptor - an evocative meditation on memory, transformation and the blurred lines between art and dream.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: World Panorama)

films.syn: In Montreal, at the dawn of the 20th century, a poor boy falls in love with a girl whose sorrow turns into pearls. He sells them to a ruthless pawnbroker, who hungers for more. Tempted by greed, the boy must choose between love and fortune. The choice could damn his soul.

films.syn: A hunter heads out to the mountains to mend his broken heart. On his way, he can’t escape the visions of his lover who left him. As he loses his mind, his dark side comes to life. The shadow guides him to hunt the mythical Goldhorn and ultimately leads him to his demise. Based on the Slovenian folktale, a story about greed and our relationship towards nature.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Focus on Slovenia)

films.syn: A dog is cheerfully watching little chicks hatching, and upon returning to his dog house he finds an egg in his bowl. He tries to take it back to the henhouse, but the chickens refuse and the Cock chases him away. Saddened, he seeks advice from the Squirrel, who trusts a dove with the egg. However, the dove is too small, so the Squirrel secretly takes the egg back to the dog. When the egg starts to vibrate, the dog gets frightened and throws it away. But with the cold and the rain comes guilt – the dog finally warms the egg with care, a happy little chick hatches next to its new dad.

films.syn: By visualising the familiar and relatable feeling of home and comparing it to life on the streets, this film explains what people with unstable living situations are missing. ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Student Film Competition)

films.t: The Pool or Death of a Goldfish
films.syn: The Pool or Death of a Goldfish is a story about a possessive relationship between a mother and her daughter. The main character, through unexpressed anger and rebellion against her mother, transforms into a titular goldfish. Unspoken words, gestures, and repressed childhood emotions manifest in harsh treatment of both herself and others. The film is framed by a compositional structure in which the main character finally allows herself to feel grief, thereby entering a process of self-acceptance and forgiveness.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: World Panorama)

films.syn: Deep underground, embedded in old muddy rock, the oracle is waiting. A big bright square tells the story of our present on repeat. Slowly it descends over small motionless people stuck in the middle of a world consuming itself. How do you want to be forgotten?

films.syn: Mount Teide is one of the world’s largest active volcanoes, and there may be a way to use the basalt rock inside it to save humanity. Obviously, destroying an ancient volcano would cause catastrophic and unpredictable ecological fallout. But what if we harvested only some of that basalt - could it really stop climate change?

films.syn: A routine work trip for married couple Hana and Kornel suddenly turns into an adventurous struggle for survival. In a remote forest, far from civilization, they are forced to face not only the wilderness, but also the fragile terrain of their long-term, stagnant relationship.

films.syn: Trade Tattoo went even further than Rainbow Dance in its experimental use of the three-colour process. This time Lye used the Technicolor system. The film is based on black and white ‘found footage’ taken from GPO Film Unit documentaries, including Night Mail. The way he transformed these images has been described as the most complex job of film printing and colour grading ever attempted. He added animated words and patterns to make the images incredibly rich and multi-layered. Music was provided by a Cuban group, the Lecuona Band. The GPO sponsored the film as publicity for the idea of ‘posting early’.

films.syn: A man journeys back in time to find his younger self, under the guise of trading cards, but the exchange turns into a haunting exploration of identity, mental health and the fading light of childhood innocence.

films.syn: In a city - evoking, without specificity, a city of the Roman Empire - the poem depicts a state of waiting: the arrival of the ‘Barbarians’ has been announced, the emperor himself seems ready to submit to their authority, and every hypothesis about the future is possible. The city holds its breath in anticipation… But who, exactly, are these ‘Barbarians’? And what if they do not come?

films.t: War of Words or the Respectful Silence?
films.syn: The short film was created within the framework of the project of the same name, aimed at exploring tools to understand the turbulent legacy of the 20th century, specifically the period between the two World Wars. It charts the path from understanding the past to comprehending the present, emphasizing the importance of speaking rather than remaining silent, and encouraging courage and openness in dialogue as keys to resolving conflicts and cohabitation.

films.syn: Dressed as the demigod Siegfried (and cutting a less than impressive figure as such), Elmer Fudd is pursuing Bugs Bunny when he finds rabbit tracks and arrives at Bugs' hole. Elmer jams his spear into the hole while singing “Kill the wabbit!” repeatedly (to the tune of Ride of the Valkyries from Die Walküre). Bugs sticks his head out from another hole and converses with Elmer about the latter's spear and magic helmet. This prompts a display of Elmer-as-Siegfried's magical powers. Bugs flees in fear, and Elmer pursues.
